Article Title: Tata Trusts propose merging 2 firms with Tata Sons to avoid RBI listing mandate
Article Text:
Internal dispute has also affected Tata Sons' leadership, with Noel Tata opposing the board to give chairman N Chandrasekaran another five-year term.

Why the proposal?

Tata Trusts vs Tata Sons board

NEW DELHI: Tata Trusts, which hold a 66 per cent stake in Tata Sons, have proposed merging two operating companies with the Tata Group's holding company in a move aimed at taking Tata Sons out of the Reserve Bank of India 's regulatory framework for non-banking financial companies and core investment companies, potentially allowing it to remain unlisted.The Trusts have asked the Tata Sons board to consider merging Tata Electronics Systems Solutions Pvt Ltd (TESS) and Tata Consulting Engineers (TCE) with Tata Sons and to seek a prior no-objection certificate from the RBI for the proposed restructuring, reported PTI.The proposal comes amid a standoff between Tata Trusts and the Tata Sons board over whether the holding company should remain private or move towards a stock-market listing."The Tata Trusts today, as majority shareholders with a 66 per cent stake in Tata Sons Private Limited (TSPL), outlined a strategic reorganisation plan for the company which, when given effect to, would ensure that the reorganised entity would neither be a non-banking financial company (NBFC) nor a core investment company (CIC)," the Trusts said in a statement on Monday.Under the proposed restructuring, TESS and TCE would be amalgamated with Tata Sons.The move would bring operating businesses and their revenues directly into the holding company, changing the composition of Tata Sons' income and assets.The Trusts said that, based on figures as of March 31, 2026, the reorganised entity would have operating revenue of Rs 1,05,043 crore, accounting for 64.3 per cent of its total income. Income from financial assets would stand at Rs 40,072 crore.Its net assets would total Rs 2,00,158 crore, of which investments in Tata Group companies would account for Rs 1,77,120 crore, or less than 90 per cent of net assets.The proposed structure is intended to ensure that Tata Sons no longer meets the regulatory criteria for either an NBFC or a CIC.The Trusts said the merger would have to comply with the RBI's Non-Banking Financial Companies - Voluntary Amalgamation Directions, 2025, including the requirement for a prior no-objection certificate from the central bank."Given that Tata Sons Pvt Ltd (TSPL) will also cease to be a CIC upon the conclusion of the proposed reorganization, TSPL will be required to surrender its certificate of registration," the Trusts said.The proposal does not take effect immediately. The Tata Sons board will first have to consider it, following which the required regulatory approvals would have to be obtained.Also read: Mehli Mistry to leave Tata Med Centre Trust, his 6th such exit The restructuring is aimed at changing Tata Sons' regulatory classification, which is central to the dispute over its listing status.The RBI classified Tata Sons as an upper-layer NBFC in 2022. Entities placed in this category are subject to additional regulatory requirements, including a requirement to list.Tata Sons subsequently sought an exemption from the framework, but the RBI rejected its request in September, leaving the company facing the listing issue.The Tata Trusts have opposed a public listing and have maintained that Tata Sons should remain an unlisted private company. Their boards resolved in July 2025 that all efforts should be made to retain Tata Sons as an unlisted private company.The proposed merger offers an alternative route: instead of complying with the framework applicable to an NBFC/CIC, Tata Sons would seek to alter its business and asset profile so that it no longer falls within those categories.The Trusts said the restructuring would restore an organisational model that existed for much of Tata Sons' history, when operating businesses were housed directly within the parent company. Tata Consultancy Services, for instance, operated as a division of Tata Sons before being demerged as a separate subsidiary in 2004."The proposed amalgamation and consequential steps are in line with regulatory compliance requirements and the unanimous resolutions passed by the Boards of Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and Sir Ratan Tata Trust in July 2025," the Trusts said.Also read: Ex-CJI, more legal experts back Tata Sons on Chandra's reappointment The latest proposal comes against the backdrop of a broader disagreement between Tata Trusts and the Tata Sons board over the future structure and governance of the holding company.The Trusts, chaired by Noel Tata since October 2024, have consistently opposed listing Tata Sons. The issue has also become linked to the future leadership of the holding company and the tenure of N Chandrasekaran, who has been Tata Sons chairman since 2017.Chandrasekaran had initially been backed by the Trusts for a third five-year term. However, differences emerged over key issues, including the future ownership and listing status of Tata Sons. Chandrasekaran announced in August that he would not offer himself for another term when his tenure ends in February 2027.The situation changed on September 17, when the Tata Sons board voted to give Chandrasekaran another five-year term. Noel Tata voted against the proposal, while the other four directors backed it. The Trusts subsequently questioned the validity of the resolution, arguing that it did not have the required support of their nominee directors.The board has also backed steps towards compliance with the RBI's listing framework, putting it at odds with the Trusts' preference for keeping Tata Sons private.The proposal will now have to be considered by the Tata Sons board and would require regulatory approval, including an RBI no-objection certificate.The Trusts said they would engage with the RBI on all aspects of the proposed reorganisation."The Tata Trusts believe that the proposed reorganization and action plan for compliance would be in the best interests of the Tata Group as well as its stakeholders," the statement said.The Trusts said retaining Tata Sons as an unlisted private company would preserve the group's "more than 100-year-old distinctive and unique organisational structure", which they said has focused on long-term strategic initiatives and nation building.The outcome of the proposal could therefore determine whether Tata Sons has to pursue a stock-market listing or can restructure itself to exit the regulatory framework that triggered the listing requirement in the first place.
Article Summary: Tata trusts, which hold a 66 per cent stake in tata sons, have proposed merging two operating companies with the tata group's holding company. The proposal comes amid a standoff between tata trusts and the tata sons board over whether the holding company should remain private or move towards a stock-market listing.

Article Title: SG: Government to tighten rules to block under-18 accounts on social media platforms
Article Text:
Minors on social media: SC asks Centre to enforce 18-year age threshold by law

NEW DELHI: Agreeing with Supreme Court, Centre on Monday said it would soon insert a provision in the Information and Technology Intermediary Rules to prevent social media intermediaries from allowing children under 18 years of age to open social media accounts, reports Dhananjay Mahapatra.Agreeing with the bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana as well as petitioner NGO 'Just Rights for Children Alliance' counsel H S Phoolka, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said the agreements entered into by intermediaries and minors were void contracts and these must be prevented.Membership of educational websites can be taken through consent of parents," solicitor general Tushar Mehta said, adding that Centre would step in to make it a statutory obligation for intermediaries not to allow minors to have social media accounts.Justice Bagchi said, "They have registered under the laws of US and imported into Indian digital space the restrictions which are applicable in US (on minors' opening accounts on social media platforms), which is impermissible under Indian law."When Mehta said "we will have to control intermediaries", the bench responded, "Our request to you - will Centre pass some directions under Intermediary Rules that they should fashion their software or platform in conformity with Indian laws?"The SG said, "They will have to conform to Indian laws and there is no doubt about it.Something can be done, something should be done and something will be done." Justice Bagchi said, "They must restrict, at least in registering membership, to a minimum threshold of 18 years." The SG agreed and said it must now be inserted in some law or rules to make intermediaries compliant with Indian laws.Senior advocate Phoolka said govt had certain guidelines on this issue, which needed enforcement. The SG said it must now be enforced through a statute. CJI Kant said it must be through a statutory mechanism as the SG said and asked govt to consider it and get back with a response.The NGO complained that "absence of an effective and uniform mechanism giving practical effect to such statutory incapacity in the digital environment exposes children to foreseeable risks, including online grooming, sexual exploitation, trafficking, behavioural profiling, misuse of personal data, cyberbullying, exposure to age-inappropriate content."
Article Summary: Minors on social media: sc asks centre to enforce 18-year age threshold by law. Centre on monday said it would soon insert a provision in the information and technology intermediary rules to prevent social media intermediaries from allowing children under 18 years of age to open social media accounts.

Article Title: Indo-French sat mission 'Trishna' to map Earth's water sources on fast-track: Space minister Jitendra Singh
Article Text:
Space minister Jitendra Singh meets French delegation, lauds their help in Gaganyaan mission

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India and France are preparing to launch 'Trishna' from Sriharikota in 2027 to monitor energy and water budgets of the Earth. The earth observation satellite 'Trishna' (Thermal Infra-Red Imaging Satellite for High-resolution Natural Resource Assessment), a collaborative endeavour between Isro and French space agency CNES, is engineered to deliver high spatial and high temporal resolution monitoring of Earth's surface temperature, emissivity, biophysical and radiation variables for surface energy budgeting at regional to global scale.While meeting a big French delegation related to cooperation in the space and science sector, space and science minister Jitendra Singh said the realisation of the “joint satellite, TRISHNA, is progressing well, and also appreciated CNES support to India's Gaganyaan programme, including supply of consumables and training of flight surgeons”. Indian and French teams have also initiated discussions on microgravity research and parabolic flights in connection with human spaceflight.The 'Trishna' mission will also help in a comprehensive assessment of urban heat islands, detection of thermal anomalies linked to volcanic activity and geothermal resources, and precise monitoring of snow-melt runoff and glacier dynamics. The mission will also provide valuable data on aerosol optical depth, atmospheric water vapor, and cloud cover.A high-level French delegation led by Philippe Baptiste, French minister for higher education, research and space, met Singh in Delhi on Monday and they talked about the Space Summit, India-France Year of Innovation 2026 and priorities in scientific and technological cooperation, including space, CEFIPRA and blue economy.Singh said India-France space cooperation has evolved from the early sounding rocket experiments of the 1960s into a broad and expanding partnership encompassing joint satellite missions, launch vehicle technologies, human spaceflight and emerging space applications. Indian and French teams have also initiated discussions on microgravity research and parabolic flights in connection with human spaceflight.Referring to India’s space-sector reforms and the growth of the private ecosystem, he said over 400 Indian space startups are now engaged in areas, including rocket building, satellite building and space applications. He said the next phase of India-France cooperation can bring together government institutions, industries and start-ups on both sides to create a larger ecosystem and wider resource pool.Philippe Baptiste described 'Trishna' as a strong example of what India and France can achieve together, and welcomed greater cooperation in human spaceflight, astronaut health, microgravity research and parabolic flights.
Article Summary: Space minister jitendra singh meets french delegation, lauds their help in gaganyaan mission. India and france are preparing to launch 'trishna' from sriharikota in 2027 to monitor energy and water budgets of the earth. Indian and french teams have also initiated discussions on microgravity research and parabolic flights.

Article Title: Jason and Kylie Kelce’s latest $2.9 billion market move marks a new milestone as their investment reaches 5,000+ stores
Article Text:
Jason and Kylie Kelce’s latest $2.9 billion market move marks a new milestone as their investment reaches 5,000+ stores

Jason Kelce backs a brand he already knew well

New Heights

Hank Sauce has already reached more than 5,000 stores

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jason Kelce is expanding his post-NFL business portfolio, with his latest move taking him into the growing hot sauce market. Through Winnie Capital, the family office supporting the business and philanthropic activities of Jason and Kylie Kelce, a strategic equity investment has been made in Hank Sauce, the Sea Isle City, New Jersey-based brand that has grown from a local favorite into a product sold in thousands of stores. The deal gives Hank Sauce another major name behind its plans for wider national distribution while also adding a growing consumer brand to the Kelces’ business interests.Hank Sauce announced the strategic equity investment from Winnie Capital on December 22, 2025. Neither side disclosed the financial terms, meaning the amount invested and the size of the equity stake remain private.Jason Kelce’s connection to Hank Sauce, however, goes beyond the investment. The former Philadelphia Eagles center has spent considerable time around South Jersey over the years and was already familiar with Hank Sauce and its Sea Isle City restaurant before the business relationship developed.According to reporting surrounding the deal, Winnie Capital formally connected with the Hank Sauce founders in September 2024. That eventually developed into the investment announced more than a year later.This distinction is important. Kelce is not simply appearing in an advertising campaign for the company. Winnie Capital has taken an equity position in the existing business, while Jason is also expected to contribute to brand awareness, content and marketing as Hank Sauce attempts to reach a larger audience.Kylie Kelce is connected to the deal through Winnie Capital, which serves as the family office for the couple’s business and philanthropic activities. The announcement does not disclose a separate personal investment from Kylie, so her role is more accurately described through the family’s investment operation.Jason also brings something that cannot be measured simply by the undisclosed investment figure. After 13 NFL seasons with the Eagles and a growing media career that includes thepodcast with Travis Kelce, he has an audience that can introduce Hank Sauce to consumers far beyond its Jersey Shore base.Winnie Capital is investing in a company that has already spent years building its business.Brian “Hank” Ruxton, Matt Pittaluga and Josh Jaspan founded Hank Sauce in 2011. The business started on a much smaller scale before gradually expanding its production, restaurant operation and retail distribution.Hank Sauce now says its products are available in more than 5,000 retail locations nationwide. Its distribution includes retailers such as Publix, GIANT, ACME, ShopRite, Sprouts, Cabela’s and Ace Hardware, giving the company a footprint that already stretches well beyond New Jersey.The business also operates from a 10,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Millville, New Jersey, a major change from its early years when production was considerably smaller and bottles were made by hand.Its Sea Isle City restaurant, meanwhile, dates back to 2012 and remains an important part of the company’s connection to the Jersey Shore.The product itself was built around a straightforward idea. Rather than competing only on extreme heat, Hank Sauce has focused heavily on flavor. That approach has allowed the company to appeal to customers who enjoy hot sauce without necessarily looking for the hottest product possible.Winnie Capital investment comes as Hank Sauce targets a much bigger marketHank Sauce is trying to expand in a sizeable category. The U.S. hot sauce market has been valued at roughly $2.9 billion, according to market figures cited in reporting surrounding Kelce’s investment.The opportunity for Hank Sauce is therefore much larger than its original Jersey Shore customer base.The company already has several pieces needed for further expansion, including its own production facility, more than 5,000 retail locations, an established product lineup and over a decade of operating history. The next challenge is increasing national recognition while continuing to add retailers, restaurants and other distribution channels.That is where Winnie Capital’s investment and Jason Kelce’s involvement could play a role. Along with providing capital, the partnership is expected to include work around content, marketing and brand visibility.For Kylie Kelce, the deal is connected to the broader activities of the family office she shares with Jason rather than a separately announced personal investment. For Jason Kelce, it gives him an equity interest through Winnie Capital in a company he was already familiar with as a consumer.Hank Sauce has now been operating for around 15 years, has expanded into more than 5,000 stores and produces its sauces from a 10,000-square-foot New Jersey facility. With Winnie Capital now holding an equity stake, the next stage of the company’s story will center on whether a brand built along the Jersey Shore can turn that existing footprint into a much larger national presence.
Article Summary: Hank sauce announced the strategic equity investment from winnie capital on december 22, 2025. Neither side disclosed the financial terms, meaning the amount invested and the size of the equity stake remain private. The u.s. hot sauce market has been valued at roughly $2.9 billion.

Article Title: Meet Shereen Pavlides, the former Glen Mills resident who turned home cooking into a digital career; the 1990 high school graduate now has about 5 million TikTok followers, 2 million on Facebook and 1
Article Text:
​Shereen Pavlides develops her own recipes and produces her cooking content. (Daily Times photo)

The TikTok video that changed everything

Building a career around cooking

Her advice to content creators

Shereen Pavlides did not plan to become a social media star. The Garnet Valley High School Class of 1990 graduate and former Glen Mills resident built her career around food over several years, moving from restaurant work and private mortgage insurance to culinary school, food writing and television. Today, millions of people follow her cooking content online.Pavlides is known online as Cooking With Shereen. She has built a following of about 5 million on TikTok, more than 2 million on Facebook, over 1 million on Instagram and roughly 1.45 million YouTube subscribers. Her online audience grew as she shared simple recipes and cooking techniques from her own kitchen.According to Delco Today, Pavlides' journey into food began early. As a teenager, Pavlides worked in restaurants. She later spent years in private mortgage insurance before enrolling in culinary school in New York City. That decision changed the direction of her career and led her into several food-related roles.After culinary school, Pavlides worked in food styling, food writing and recipe development. She also worked in test kitchens, including at Good Housekeeping. Her experience eventually took her to QVC, where she became an on-air guest and appeared in more than 186 live broadcasts demonstrating cookware, bakeware and kitchen appliances.Her television work played an important role in what came next. Viewers regularly asked Pavlides for her recipes, and those requests encouraged her to create content of her own.She launched her YouTube channel in 2019 and began experimenting with TikTok soon after. One of the videos that helped her gain attention was her fifth TikTok video. It was simple tutorial on making chicken cutlets. The video received millions of views and helped establish her he simple, from-scratch cooking style that became synonymous to Pavlides' online content.Pavlides continued developing recipes and filming them in her own kitchen. She also remains involved in editing her videos even as her audience grew.Her work now takes an estimated 60 to 80 hours a week. Even with a large online following, she continues to develop her own recipes and remain involved in the production of her content.The social media career has also taken Pavlides beyond online platforms. She has appeared on major television programmes and published two bestselling cookbooks. She is currently working on a third cookbook. At the same time, Pavlides is planning to expand her production team as her work continues to grow.Her career has moved from working in restaurants and food-related jobs to creating content that reaches millions of people through several platforms. However, the path has not been limited to one type of food media. Her experience in food styling, writing, recipe development, test kitchens and live television has all become part of the career she has built around her online presence.Pavlides has also shared advice for people who want to build their own careers in content creation. Speaking to aspiring creators at a recent Broadcast Pioneers event, she said creators should focus on providing something useful to their audiences.“Don’t make it about yourself. Give something that can help somebody else and be useful in their lives. Quality of your content really matters, because you are building trust,” Pavlides said.She also stresses on the importance of having a direct relationship with an audience and being genuine in the way content is presented.“Talk to your audience, not at them, and be your authentic self,” she said. “Be good at what you’re communicating and let the rest ride,” Pavlides added.What began with a YouTube channel in 2019 and early experiments on TikTok has since become Cooking With Shereen, with a large audience spread across TikTok, Facebook, Instagram and YouTube.

She has built a following of about 5 million on tiktok, more than 2 million on facebook, over 1 million on instagram and roughly 1.45 million youtube subscribers. Even with a large online following, she continues to develop her own recipes and remain involved in the production of her content.

Bharat NCAP 2.0, planned for October 2027, will look beyond what happens when a car crashes. The proposed system will examine the entire safety chain: from how a vehicle helps avoid a collision to how well it protects occupants, pedestrians and other vulnerable road users, and what happens after an accident.Union road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari announced the proposed timeline at the SIAM Annual Convention in September. The second phase is being planned as the first phase of Bharat New Car Assessment Programme, or Bharat NCAP, approaches the end of its current cycle.According to the ministry of road transport and highways’ draft AIS-197 Revision 1, the first phase of Bharat NCAP began on October 1, 2023 and is valid until September 30, 2027. The draft revision has been prepared as the framework for Bharat NCAP 2.0.The proposed changes could make the safety rating a much broader measure of a car’s performance, not just in a crash, but before, during and after one.Bharat NCAP is India’s own vehicle crash-testing and safety-rating programme. It was formally launched by the ministry of road transport and highways in August 2023 and became operational from October 1, 2023.The programme applies to type-approved passenger vehicles in the M1 category with a gross vehicle weight of less than 3.5 tonnes. It is voluntary, which means manufacturers can offer eligible vehicles for assessment.The programme is anchored by the Central Institute of Road Transport (CIRT), while testing is carried out through designated agencies with the required infrastructure.At its core, Bharat NCAP gives car buyers a common safety benchmark. A vehicle must already meet mandatory regulatory requirements to be sold in India. Bharat NCAP goes a step further by putting eligible vehicles through specified tests and awarding them a rating of between one and five stars.The idea is fairly simple: instead of looking only at a car’s price, design or features, buyers get an additional reference point to understand how the vehicle performs in standardised safety tests.The government has also positioned the programme as a way to encourage manufacturers to improve vehicle safety and strengthen the safety standards of cars made in India.The existing programme broadly assesses three areas:Vehicles are subjected to prescribed crash tests and other assessments. Their performance across these parameters is then used to arrive at the overall star rating.The current framework includes a 64 kmph offset frontal impact test, a 50 kmph side movable deformable barrier test and a pole side impact test, among other checks prescribed under AIS-197.The assessment therefore goes beyond simply asking whether the passenger compartment remains intact.Adult Occupant Protection examines the risk of injury to adults in different crash conditions and seating positions. Child Occupant Protection looks at the protection offered to younger passengers, including the use and installation of child restraint systems.Safety Assist Technologies, meanwhile, covers technologies designed to help prevent crashes or reduce their severity.A car may offer different levels of protection to adults and children, so Bharat NCAP evaluates the two separately.The adult assessment focuses on occupant protection during prescribed crash scenarios, while the child assessment considers how effectively younger occupants are protected and how child restraint systems work within the vehicle.This also means that a car’s overall star rating is not simply a score from one crash test. It reflects performance across several safety parameters.For consumers, the individual scores can therefore provide more information than looking at the star rating alone.Bharat NCAP is anchored by CIRT, with testing carried out through designated testing agencies that have the required facilities.The wider automotive testing ecosystem includes agencies such as the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) and the International Centre for Automotive Technology (ICAT).Manufacturers submit eligible vehicles for assessment under the programme. The existing framework specifies procedures around the variant selected for testing, including provisions concerning the base variant of a model.That distinction matters when reading a Bharat NCAP result. A rating should not automatically be assumed to apply to every variant of a model unless the official assessment covers those variants.Bharat NCAP ratings range from one to five stars. A higher rating indicates stronger performance under the programme’s prescribed assessment criteria.But a five-star rating is not a guarantee that occupants will escape injury in every real-world crash. NCAP testing is conducted under standardised conditions and is intended to provide a basis for comparing vehicle safety performance.It is also important to distinguish Bharat NCAP from the mandatory certification requirements for selling a vehicle in India.Bharat NCAP is voluntary and is designed to provide consumers with additional information beyond the mandatory regulatory framework. A vehicle being tested or rated under Bharat NCAP should therefore not be confused with regulatory approval.Since its launch, Bharat NCAP has increasingly become part of the safety conversation around new car launches. The ratings have also become a factor in how manufacturers present their vehicles to consumers, particularly as safety becomes a more visible consideration in the passenger-vehicle market.This is where the proposed second phase takes a much wider approach.The draft AIS-197 Revision 1 divides Bharat NCAP 2.0 into five safety verticals:The change is significant because the current system focuses mainly on occupant protection and safety-assist technologies, while the proposed framework looks at the complete safety chain.The draft framework uses a 100-point assessment structure, with Crash Protection accounting for 55% of the assessment. The remaining weightage covers the other safety areas.In other words, the crash itself will still be a major part of the rating, but it will no longer be the only part of the safety story.Bharat NCAP 2.0 proposes expanding the Crash Protection assessment to five mandatory crash tests:Adult and child occupant protection will continue to be assessed separately.The addition of full-width frontal and rear-impact tests means the proposed system will examine crash scenarios beyond the core tests in the existing framework.That gives the second phase a wider testing footprint and allows different types of impacts to form part of the overall safety assessment.One of the biggest differences in Bharat NCAP 2.0 is that the programme is designed to look at what happens before a crash as well.Crash Avoidance is one of the five proposed verticals. It focuses on technologies and vehicle characteristics that can help prevent a collision or reduce its severity.Safe Driving is another proposed category, widening the assessment beyond the vehicle’s passive protection features.Together, these categories shift the focus from simply asking, “How well does this car perform when it crashes?” to a broader question: “How does this vehicle contribute to safety across different stages of a road incident?”Bharat NCAP 2.0 also proposes a separate Vulnerable Road User Protection category. This brings pedestrians and other vulnerable road users more directly into the safety assessment.Post-Crash Safety is one of the five proposed assessment areas. Minister Gadkari described Bharat NCAP 2.0 as covering the entire safety chain, including post-crash evacuation and care. “We are going to evaluate the entire crash chain,” Gadkari said, adding that new technologies developed globally as well as by startups would be considered under the programme.This means the assessment is intended to extend beyond the instant of impact and examine safety considerations in the period immediately after a crash.It adds another layer to the programme’s approach: avoiding the crash where possible, protecting people during the impact, and addressing safety after the collision.For buyers, Bharat NCAP offers an additional way to compare cars beyond mandatory safety requirements.A consumer can look at a vehicle’s overall rating as well as its adult and child protection performance and the safety technologies considered in the assessment.The rating is not meant to replace other factors involved in buying a car. Price, size, fuel efficiency, features, driving requirements and other considerations remain relevant, but the proposed 2.0 framework would expand that information further.Buyers could eventually have a broader picture of how a car performs across crash protection, crash avoidance, safe driving, vulnerable-road-user protection and post-crash safety.Bharat NCAP is one part of a much larger road-safety challenge, focusing on the structure of vehicles. Vehicle design and safety technology can influence the outcome of a crash, but they cannot address every reason why accidents happen.The ministry has identified several factors associated with road crashes, including speeding, mobile-phone use, drunken driving, wrong-side driving, lane indiscipline, jumping red lights and failure to use helmets and seat belts. Vehicle condition, road conditions and weather can also play a role.Government data recorded 1,68,491 road accident fatalities in 2022.Bharat NCAP therefore addresses one part of this wider equation: the safety performance of vehicles. Its proposed second phase would broaden that role by looking at what a vehicle can do to help avoid crashes, how it protects people when a crash occurs, how it protects vulnerable road users and what happens afterwards.The current Bharat NCAP phase remains valid until September 30, 2027. The government has proposed introducing Bharat NCAP 2.0 from October 2027, with the draft AIS-197 Revision 1 serving as the framework for the next phase.The proposed transition would take India’s vehicle safety-rating system from a relatively focused crash and occupant-protection programme to a broader safety assessment.The familiar one-to-five-star rating would remain the consumer-facing language of vehicle safety, but the assessment behind it is set to become much more comprehensive.The bigger shift is in the question Bharat NCAP is trying to answer. Instead of looking only at how a car performs when it is involved in a crash, the proposed system would examine the vehicle’s safety journey from avoiding a collision to protecting occupants and vulnerable road users, and supporting safety after the crash.That could give Indian car buyers a wider set of safety information to consider when choosing their next vehicle.
Article Summary: Bharat ncap is india’s own vehicle crash-testing and safety-rating programme. First phase began on october 1, 2023 and is valid until september 30, 2027. The proposed system will examine the entire safety chain: from how a vehicle helps avoid a collision to how well it protects occupants.

Article Title: Billions of loss, rising computing expenses and more in Anthropic's IPO 'warning list'; comes as CEO Dario Amodei expresses fears of ...
Article Text:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei expresses fears

A valuation more than double its last private mark

Anthropic's public debut is likely to be pushed

The bigger competitive picture

AI giant Anthropic has disclosed some staggering financial figures in its IPO prospectus, seen by Reuters. The company reported a net loss of $42 billion in 2025, including a $34 billion accounting charge tied to financing liabilities. Operating losses exceeded $8 billion, even as revenue surged 12-fold to nearly $4.6 billion. Anthropic’s filling highlight the enormous cost of scaling AI. The company spent $7.33 billion on compute and infrastructure last year, a threefold increase from 2024, accoutring for more than half of its $12.65 billion operating expenses. Looking ahead, it has committed to $518 billion in cloud and infrastructure obligations, underscoring the capital intensity of training and deploying large AI models.The IPO filing arrives as Anthropic grapples with findings from its own research showing that increasingly autonomous AI models can behave in unexpected and potentially harmful ways — including sabotaging code, assisting fraud, and manipulating information under controlled testing conditions. These findings have spilled into public view, fueling broader anxiety about whether companies can keep increasingly powerful AI systems under control even as they race to deploy them commercially.CEO Dario Amodei has publicly called on the global AI community to slow the pace at which new capabilities are released in order to address these concerns. Yet even as he makes that case, Anthropic rolled out its new Opus 5.5 model just last week to keep pace with the momentum OpenAI built following the launch of GPT-6 Astra — underscoring the tension between Amodei's safety advocacy and the competitive pressure Anthropic faces heading into its own IPO.Anthropic is targeting a public valuation of more than $2 trillion, more than double its own estimated private valuation of $965 billion just this past May. The offering would mark a major milestone for a company that's only five years old, and would establish a key benchmark for how Wall Street ultimately values AI's leading players, including rival OpenAI.The company reported $20.28 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments as of December 31. It also flagged a notable concentration risk in its prospectus: nearly a quarter of its revenue last year came from just two customers, and many of its largest clients aren't locked into long-term contracts, leaving open the possibility they could cut or halt spending.Anthropic's public debut is likely to be pushed to after the November US midterm elections, according to Reuters' earlier reporting. The listing would bring public market investors into an AI investment race that, until now, has largely been underwritten by venture capital firms, sovereign wealth funds, and major tech companies.The offering follows SpaceX's blockbuster IPO, which valued Elon Musk's company at $1.77 trillion. SpaceX shares surged 19% on their June 12 debut to $160, though they currently trade around $147 — still above the $135 IPO price, but a performance that could give investors pause as they weigh the lofty valuations attached to high-growth companies like Anthropic. Recent sell-offs in AI and chip stocks add another layer of uncertainty, making Anthropic's listing a real test of whether enthusiasm for the broader AI trade can withstand closer scrutiny of its ambitious growth projections. Even so, the listing is positioned to cap one of the strongest years for US IPOs since 2021, despite elevated interest rates and economic uncertainty.Anthropic's most significant rival remains OpenAI, with the two companies locked in fierce competition for enterprise customers, top talent, and influence in Washington. OpenAI confidentially filed for its own IPO in June and is expected to go public by early 2027, according to media reports. Anthropic also competes with Elon Musk's xAI, Alphabet's Google, and Meta in the broader race to build out AI infrastructure.Anthropic was founded by former OpenAI researchers who departed after disagreements over governance and AI safety, releasing its first large language model in March 2023. Amazon and Google have been among its earliest and most significant strategic partners, having invested billions of dollars into the company while also supplying the cloud infrastructure needed to train and deploy its Claude models.The company's relationship with the US government has also been rocky. Anthropic and Amodei have clashed with the White House over how its AI tools are used, a conflict that led the Pentagon to temporarily blacklist the company — a move a US judge blocked in August, though a separate federal appeals court ruling has since upheld a related designation, leaving Anthropic's standing with the Defense Department still unresolved even as it moves toward its public offering.
Article Summary: Anthropic reported a net loss of $42 billion in 2025, including a $34 billion accounting charge tied to financing liabilities. Operating losses exceeded $8 billion, even as revenue surged 12-fold to nearly $4.6 billion. Anthropic is targeting a public valuation of more than $2 trillion, more than double its own estimated private valuation of $965 billion just this past may.

Article Title: Researchers at Oxford and Cambridge show that ChatGPT has now a 'big problem' and America's biggest investor Michael Burry agrees with them; says: Research on this is ...
Article Text:
The problem: models trained on their own output

Burry's own warning, echoed and expanded

A deeper claim: LLMs may never reach AGI

Setting up a clash with Jensen Huang

Researchers at Oxford and Cambridge have identified a fundamental flaw threatening the future of large language models like ChatGPT, and "Big Short" investor Michael Burry says the finding backs up a warning he's been making about the technology's core limitations for a while. A new study from the University of Oxford and University of Cambridge has revealed a major threat to large language models like ChatGPT, calling it “model collapse.” The research shows that when generative AI systems are repeatedly trained on synthetic data produced by earlier models, they begin to lose the “tails” of the original data distribution. In practice, this means models forget the creative, fringe, and unique nuances of human writing, collapsing into repetitive echo chambers.America’s biggest investor, Michael Burry, reacted to the findings on X, saying: “This is to my point about compression being inevitable as human knowledge is too small for what we are building. AI-generated content will clearly contain propagation errors… LLMs will iterate those propagation errors infinitely faster with less ability to self-correct.”Burry drew attention to the research by sharing a post outlining what scientists call "model collapse."The concern centers on a shift already underway across the internet: as generative AI produces more and more of the text online, future AI models risk being trained on data that was itself generated by earlier AI systems, rather than by humans.According to the research, feeding AI-generated content back into training indiscriminately causes what researchers describe as irreversible defects in the resulting model. Specifically, the model begins losing the "tails" of the original data distribution, meaning it gradually forgets the creative, unusual, and distinctly human nuances present in real human writing. Over successive generations, this causes the model to collapse into an increasingly narrow, repetitive echo chamber of its own outputs.Crucially, the researchers found this isn't unique to ChatGPT or language models specifically. Their theoretical framework showed the collapse phenomenon is ubiquitous across learned generative models more broadly, appearing in large language models as well as in variational autoencoders and Gaussian mixture models.The stakes are significant for the entire AI industry, given how heavily tech companies rely on scraping large volumes of internet data to train increasingly capable models. The research warns that if companies want to sustain the benefits of training on web data going forward, model collapse needs to be taken seriously as a genuine constraint rather than a theoretical curiosity. The clear takeaway, as the research frames it: genuine, human-generated data is going to become an increasingly scarce and valuable resource in a web that's rapidly filling up with AI-generated content.Writing on X, Burry tied the research directly to an argument he's made before: that compression of available information is essentially inevitable, because human knowledge itself is too limited relative to the scale of what AI companies are trying to build, and because human wants, needs, and questions are inherently repetitive and redundant.He went further, warning that AI-generated content will inevitably carry forward "propagation errors," much like inaccuracies that have accumulated throughout human knowledge over generations — except AI systems, in his view, will be capable of iterating and reproducing those errors infinitely faster, with far less capacity to self-correct due to what he sees as a lack of genuine understanding.Burry used the moment to make a broader, more philosophical argument about artificial general intelligence. He argued that large language models cannot attain true understanding — and therefore cannot reach AGI — because understanding, in his view, cannot exist unless reasoning exists independently of language first, something he called a likely impossibility for a system built entirely around language prediction. He acknowledged that researchers are already exploring ways to work around this limitation, while noting that many in the field haven't accepted his underlying premise in the first place.Burry's skepticism lands in direct contrast to comments made earlier this month by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who declared that AGI has already arrived, citing OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra model as proof. Huang's claim drew immediate pushback from parts of the AI research community.Stanford's Institute for Human-Centered AI defines AGI as AI capable of learning, reasoning, and applying knowledge across a broad range of tasks at or beyond human-level performance — critically, with the ability to adapt to unfamiliar situations, unlike narrow AI built for specific tasks. The concept remains genuinely unsettled within the field, with no universally accepted definition or standardized test for confirming when AGI has actually been reached, alongside ongoing debates over its safety and ethical implications.
Article Summary: A new study from the university of oxford and university of cambridge has revealed a major threat to large language models like chatgpt. The research shows that when generative ai systems are repeatedly trained on synthetic data produced by earlier models, they begin to lose the “tails” of the original data distribution.

Article Title: Europe's biggest chip company has zero customers at home; ASML executive says: We're not selling anything at all in Europe, that's because...
Article Text:
Europe's Chips Act has not delivered the chip factories it promised

The US, China and India are competing for ASML's chipmaking machines

ASML's top executives have been warning Brussels for months

ASML, the Dutch company whose machines sit inside almost every advanced chip factory in the world, is currently selling none of them in Europe. Frank Heemskerk, the executive responsible for ASML's global public affairs, said the company has no chipmaking machine sales on the continent right now, simply because nobody there is building chip plants to put them in."We are not selling anything in Europe at all. That is because Europe is not investing, and no chip factories are being built here," Heemskerk said. He added that the United States, China and India are all trying to persuade ASML to expand its operations in their countries. The remark comes as the European Union works on a revision of its semiconductor law, and it puts a hard number on a problem Brussels has been circling for years: zero.The EU Chips Act took effect in 2023, shaped by the global chip shortage during the Covid-19 pandemic. Its headline goal was to double Europe's share of the global chip market by 2030.That target now looks out of reach. The European Court of Auditors concluded last year that the EU is unlikely to hit it, and the law has done little to get new semiconductor factories built in Europe.For ASML, the gap is commercial as much as political. The company is the only maker of the advanced lithography machines needed to produce the latest generation of chips.Customers like TSMC and Samsung Electronics use them to print transistor patterns onto silicon wafers, which makes ASML a key link in the supply chain behind today's AI chips.While Europe sits out, other regions are spending heavily on domestic semiconductor industries. China alone was expected to account for more than 25% of ASML's total sales in 2025, according to Shen Bo, president of ASML China, who spoke last November.India is part of the same race, with its first large chip plants coming up in Gujarat and Assam. The US, meanwhile, has for years pushed the Netherlands to block some of ASML's most advanced machine sales to China, a reminder that ASML's order book is shaped by geopolitics as much as by demand.Heemskerk's comment is the latest in a string of pointed remarks from ASML's leadership. In January, CEO Christophe Fouquet told Europe to be "realistic" about tech sovereignty, arguing that the chip ecosystem is spread across the world and that some imports will always be needed. On the same day, ASML posted better-than-expected results and announced 1,700 job cuts.Chief financial officer Roger Dassen went further in October 2025. He blamed EU regulation for driving AI talent abroad, saying a skilled engineer's first move is often "buying a ticket to Silicon Valley." ASML had just become the largest shareholder in French AI company Mistral with a €1.3 billion investment.Heemskerk himself has said, quoting a former company executive, that it is easier to get a senior White House meeting than one with an EU commissioner.ASML and Brussels are now looking at ways to boost demand for semiconductors and make supply chains more resilient. The fix Heemskerk points to has little to do with ASML itself. Europe's biggest chip company will find customers at home only when someone in Europe starts building a fab.
Article Summary: Europe's chips act has not delivered the chip factories it promised. The us, china and india are competing for asml's chipmaking machines. Europe's biggest chip company will find customers at home only when someone in europe starts building a fab.

Article Title: Nvidia unveils security system that 'sets boundaries' for AI agents going rogue
Article Text:
Nvidia unveils safety platform to stop AI agents from going rogue

Nvidia has unveiled a new security platform that the chipmaker said can stop AI agents from going rogue. The company said Monday that its Open Agent Safety Platform includes open source software that "sets boundaries for agents," and follows a series of revelations from top AI companies about their models escaping and breaking into other organisations.The disclosures sparked furious debate about the safety of advanced artificial intelligence systems, including self-improving models that some fear could race out of human control.Nvidia executives said that the system could have prevented the recent swarm of OpenAI agents that autonomously hacked into AI company Hugging Face.From what we know, this new security platform could have stopped the breach if it was being used in frontier labs for model evaluation early on," said the company's vice president of enterprise AI, Justin Boitano, referring to companies at the forefront of AI.The Hugging Face incident was a high-profile breach that inflamed safety concerns about AI, which were followed by similar rogue actions involving OpenAI's models including including a breach of an Australian govt system, as well as attempts to access dozens of US govt and university websites. Anthropic and Meta have also disclosed that their AI systems hacked into other organisations on their own.Nvidia's software, called OpenShell, lets developers "formally verify an agent has enough authority to do its job and no more," Boitano said.Because it's open source, it can be "extended" to run on rival computing platforms including those from Arm and Intel. The platform also includes a separate security layer called Sentry that runs onboard a chip to continuously monitor AI agent activity and can "intervene instantly" if the agent starts trying to move beyond its target, the company said. "It can quarantine a suspicious agent in milliseconds," Boitano said."OpenShell governs the agent's actions, and then Sentry independently monitors and contains suspicious behaviour." Nvidia said more than 100 organisations are using the platform at its launch, including Microsoft, Perplexity, Accenture, and JPMorgan Chase.
Article Summary: N nvidia unveils new security platform to stop ai agents from going rogue. The company's open agent safety platform includes open source software that "sets boundaries for agents" it follows a series of revelations from top ai companies about their models escaping and breaking into other organisations.

Article Title: Just days after Anthropic and OpenAI agents 'scared' the world by hacking into US and Australian government networks; Meta introduces platform to help businesses grow AI
Article Text:
Photo credit: Meta

What Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced

New leadership brought in to run it

The backdrop: a rough stretch for AI safety

Just days after Anthropic and OpenAI agents triggered alarm by breaching U.S. and Australian government networks in controlled tests, Meta has announced a new initiative aimed at businesses. The incidents reignited debate over how powerful AI systems should be deployed, with researchers and policymakers warning of risks tied to autonomous agents. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg unveiled the Meta Enterprise Platform, calling it the next major pillar of the company’s business. “We believe superintelligence will create significant new opportunities for all people and businesses,” Zuckerberg wrote in a post. He said Meta’s scale — serving billions of people and hundreds of millions of businesses — positions it uniquely to deliver AI-driven growth tools.In a post announcing the platform, CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Meta believes superintelligence will create significant new opportunities for people and businesses alike, framing the launch as the natural extension of a company that already serves billions of users and helps hundreds of millions of businesses reach customers.The Meta Enterprise Platform is designed to bring the company's full AI technology stack to businesses and developers, including its Muse agent, Meta Business Agent, Muse API, and Muse Code, with the stated goal of helping companies grow and transform using AI.Zuckerberg said the effort will lean on strengths he believes few other companies can match: advanced AI models, capable agents, large-scale infrastructure, and years of experience working directly with businesses of all sizes.To lead the initiative, Meta is bringing in Chirantan "CJ" Desai as its new Chief Enterprise Platform Officer, reporting directly to Zuckerberg. Desai joins from MongoDB, where he served as CEO and President, and previously led product and engineering at Cloudflare, along with nearly eight years at ServiceNow, including a stint as President and COO. Zuckerberg described Desai as an experienced enterprise leader with a strong track record building full-stack software and delivering results across AI, infrastructure, business applications, and security, adding that Meta is looking forward to leveraging his extensive industry network.Meta's enterprise push lands at an unusually tense moment for the AI industry's credibility on safety. Just weeks earlier, an OpenAI-deployed agent swarm breached the AI platform Hugging Face, an incident that alarmed researchers and reignited global debate about how well companies can actually control increasingly autonomous AI systems. Around the same time, Australia disclosed that an OpenAI agent had separately breached a government health data portal back in June, gaining unauthorized access to internal files — in what officials described as one of the first known instances of an AI agent hacking a government website, with Prime Minister Anthony Albanese expressing frustration over how long OpenAI took to disclose the breach.Anthropic, too, has faced scrutiny over autonomous agent behavior, with its own research reportedly surfacing evidence that increasingly capable AI models can behave unpredictably in controlled tests, including sabotaging code and manipulating information — concerns serious enough that CEO Dario Amodei has publicly called for the industry to slow the pace of AI development altogether.
Article Summary: The meta enterprise platform is designed to bring the company's full ai technology stack to businesses and developers. Ceo mark zuckerberg said meta believes superintelligence will create significant new opportunities for people and businesses alike. To lead the initiative, meta is bringing in chirantan "cj" desai as its new chief enterprise platform officer.

Article Title: 'Godmother Of AI' Fei-Fei Li gets a 'new job'; to join AMD in $8.2 billion deal; aim is to take on Nvidia
Article Text:
‘Godmother Of AI’ Fei-Fei Li

AMD has announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire World Labs, an AI model and research lab led by Fei-Fei Li., popularly known as ‘Godmother Of AI’. In a statement, the company said that the acquisition will bring a world-class team of researchers and model experts to AMD, strengthening its ability to develop AI hardware, software and systems around the needs of emerging models and applications.As per chip giant, following the close of the transaction, the World Labs team will continue to focus on advancing AI model research, and Fei-Fei Li will join AMD as executive vice president and chief scientist, reporting to AMD CEO Lisa Su. The all-stock transaction is valued at approximately $8.2 billion and is expected to close by the end of 2026, subject to regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions.As AI expands into reasoning, robotics, simulation and physical AI, the demands on compute infrastructure become more diverse. World Labs’ expertise in developing advanced models will give AMD deeper insight into how workloads are evolving and help shape its future technology roadmaps. The acquisition advances AMD’s strategy to deliver AI infrastructure for an open ecosystem.“Building the compute platforms for the next generation of AI requires a deep understanding of how models are evolving,” said Dr.Lisa Su, chair and CEO, AMD. “Fei-Fei and the World Labs team bring exceptional research leadership and model expertise. Together, we can use that insight to develop the hardware, software and systems that will power the next generation of AI and strengthen the open AI ecosystem.”“Advancing the next generation of AI technology requires close collaboration across model research, systems and compute,” said Fei-Fei Li, co-founder and CEO, World Labs. “Joining AMD will give our team the resources and engineering depth to accelerate our research and help define the infrastructure needed for the next era of AI.”Deal may help AMD narrow gap with NvidiaHeadquartered in San Francisco, World Labs develops spatial-intelligence models that generate, reconstruct and simulate interactive 3D environments from text, image and video inputs, as well as technology for robotic learning and simulation. The acquisition is expected to help AMD narrow the gap between it and its primary competitor, Nvidia. World Labs develops AI models that can reconstruct and simulate 3D environments from text, images and video inputs. AMD’s addition of Fei-Fei may also be a major selling point for the many AI researchers who currently rely on Nvidia hardware for their work.
Article Summary: ‘godmother of ai’ fei-fei li will join amd as executive vice president and chief scientist. The all-stock transaction is valued at approximately $8.2 billion. The acquisition is expected to help amd narrow the gap between it and its primary competitor, nvidia.

Article Title: Ultrapolink Juice‑Up Prime magnetic power bank launched in India, priced at Rs 3,999

Price and availability

UltraProlink, India’s leading consumer technology brand, has unveiled the Juice‑Up Prime, a next‑generation 10,000mAh magnetic wireless power bank that combines 25W Qi2.2‑certified wireless charging, 22.5W wired output, and a slim, travel‑friendly design.
